metas.name: Architecture - 3D Tiles
metas.note: Houses made of decorative, colourful, 3D tiles are sometimes found in the northwest and Caraș-Severin county.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Arches
metas.note: Towns and villages in the southern plains are often identifiable by how often you’ll find houses with arches, either supplementing walls or as an extension over a veranda or entrance. There is also a separate cluster in the hills of western Bacău county.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Banat Houses
metas.note: In Banat and to a lesser extent the rest of the flat west, you can find a distinct architecture consisting of relatively plain houses, perpendicular to the street, with two small rectangular windows on the gable. More complex Dutch-like gables and brick-lined edges are even more unique to this area.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Baroque Houses
metas.note: Less commonly in the Banat region you can find similar houses with interesting and unique baroque-style roof shapes.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Beige Stones
metas.note: In northern Cluj county you can sometimes find these thin, messy beige stones used as a construction material for walls and houses.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Bistrița Houses
metas.note: Bistrița houses often have the narrower side facing the street, with the distinctive feature being the roof flap across the gable, a feature not found in western houses.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Black Tiles
metas.note: In Suceava county you can often find black plastic roof tiles, mimicking the general trend of northern mountainous counties having darker roofs in general. These are not unique to Suceava, but are far more common there, so it is generally recommended to use this meta if you see more than one house with such a roof.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Brick Edges
metas.note: Also in the western plains of Romania you will commonly find buildings with these small bricks lining the ends of roofs. These are also found commonly in Caraș-Severin county.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Bucovina Patterns
metas.note: Bucovina is a historical region that roughly corresponds to Suceava county. This specific style of decoration along the borders of walls and windows is a feature of Bucovina architecture.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Caraş-Severin Houses
metas.note: In Caraş-Severin, you will very commonly find houses connected and lined parallel to the street, giving a more closed feel. This is a very good way of identifying the county, especially in combination with wooded hills surroundings.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Cluj Jesus
metas.note: In Cluj county you will very often find this specific style of cross planted in people’s front gardens or by the roadside. It is distinctive for its decorated semi-circular arch above the statuette.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Concrete Bollards
metas.note: Specifically in the southern part of Székely Land, in Covasna county, these concrete bollards with a ball on top are common at property entrances.
metas.footer: Note: Sometimes the ball on top is missing.

metas.name: Architecture - Constanța & Tulcea Stone Walls
metas.note: In the far southeast it is common to find stone walls or wall bases in villages, often painted white.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Corrugated Roofs
metas.note: Dark coloured, corrugated metal roofs are extremely common in Maramureș. Note they are not unique to the county, but Maramureș is the only area where they are dominant.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Crocodile Tiling
metas.note: These crocodile-scale wall tiles are common in northern, mountainous parts of the country, particularly in Maramureș and Suceava.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Danube Delta
metas.note: Tulcea county, especially around the Danube delta, has very distinct Lipovan-Russian architecture. The key elements are thatched roofs, sky-blue elements anywhere on the house, and carved wooden gables with finials.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Decorated Gables
metas.note: Intricate wooden carvings can be found as gable ornaments in a band stretching from Cluj county to the mountains bordering Neamț county.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - East Carpathian Barns
metas.note: In parts of the Eastern Carpathians you can find these barns with a wooden top part that is wider than the bottom, with vertical planks, often with thin openings.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Fence Benches
metas.note: Small covered benches integrated in fences, usually next to a gate, are common in an area covering Cluj and Sălaj counties.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Fence Tops
metas.note: Fences with a wide metal cover on top are super common in the northeast and Maramureș. Note that while they can be found occasionally outside these areas, streets completely lined with these fences will usually be in the northeast, particularly nearer the mountains in Neamț and Bacău counties.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Flaky Tiles
metas.note: These small, often flaky-looking black roof tiles can be found in the southern and eastern foothills of the Carpathians.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Fortified Churches
metas.note: Fortified churches are a feature of numerous towns and villages in formerly Transylvania Saxon populated parts of Central Romania, as well as Székely land.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Hat Roofs
metas.note: In Neamț county you can sometimes find these ‘elongated onion’ variants of hat roofs above the entrance of houses.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Indented Roofs
metas.note: Indented, mansard-like roofs are found throughout northwestern Romania. In certain regions like the Apuseni foothills, they are the dominant roof type.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Maramureș Barns
metas.note: In the southwestern part of Maramureș county (south of Baia Mare) you will find barns with particularly ornately-carved wooden walls and gables.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Maramureş Churches
metas.note:
Maramureş has a lot of wooden churches, with black-tiled roofs and particularly tall spires. The unusually tall spires can also be found on non-wooden churches in the region.

Wooden churches can also be found in the Apuseni mountains, however these are usually more modest.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Maramureș Gable
metas.note: These specific wooden gable features, often consisting of downward-pointing pikes in a row forming a small triangle at the top of the gable, are a feature of Maramureș architecture, particularly in the eastern half of the county.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Maramureș Gates
metas.note: In Maramureș you can find many intricately carved wooden gates at the entrance of properties.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Maramureș Wells
metas.note: In Maramureş county, it is common to find small circular/octagonal wells with conical roofs on people’s properties.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Maramureș Wood Houses
metas.note: Houses made entirely of wood, especially dark-coloured wood, can be found in most mountainous areas but are by far most common in eastern Maramureș county.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Metal Ornamentation
metas.note: In the east, especially the northeast, it is very common to find metal ornamentation of various types on roofs and under gables. Metal roofs in general are also more common in these regions, but are common enough in the south to be unreliable as a meta.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Modern Maramureș Gates
metas.note: Further east in Maramureș, you can often find more modern-style gates consisting of a black frame with corrugated metal sheets. Within this frame you can find many different patterns.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Moldavian Churches
metas.note: The Moldavia region (the northeast bordering Moldova) builds its churches in a distinct style. The key distinctive feature is the large semicircle ‘skirt’ roof along the back, with two smaller semicircles on the side, and a ‘witch’s hat’ roof on the spire also being quite common.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Mosque
metas.note: There is a Turkish minority along the Bulgarian border in Constanța county, which is the only significant muslim minority in Romania. You won’t find bilingual signs, however the Turkish presence is most apparent through the presence of mosques in Constanta and Tulcea County.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Neamț-Bacău Gates
metas.note: Neamț and Bacău counties have more simple versions of Suceava gates, usually missing the crossbeam underneath or the ornamentation, but still with decorated metal roofs. In Bacău especially you can find the curved variant of these roofs.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Oath Crosses
metas.note: In the Șușița and Gilort valleys in Gorj county, you will find these traditional oath crosses in many places. These are distinct small wooden crosses with a triangular top, often with writing on them and occurring in groups.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Roma Kastellos
metas.note: Wealthier Romani neighbourhoods are extremely noticeable for the over-the-top architecture, commonly featuring stacked hat roofs, sharp modern patterning, silver/gold gates and statues, and supersized versions of traditional houses even in small villages.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Roof Extensions
metas.note: Roofs with an extension that slopes lower than the roof itself are a moderately reliable meta for the east, but note that they can be found in the rest of the southern plain.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Roof Shoulders
metas.note: Roof shoulders (small tiled extensions either side of a roof end) are common in certain clusters throughout western Romania which can be helpful for a more precise regionguess.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Round Corners
metas.note: In Mureș county you can sometimes find houses where one of the front corners is rounded, often with some kind of crown or small tower above it.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Rounded Stones
metas.note: In Hunedoara you can often find these more rounded stones as a construction material for walls or house foundations.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Sheet Metal Fences
metas.note: These plain, thin, metal sheets in place of fences are a good indicator of the east, although they can also be found less prominently throughout the southern plain.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Shingle Roofs
metas.note: These shingled roofs are also a meta for the northern mountains, particularly in western Suceava. Unusually steep roofs such as the one in the image are also indicative of the same area.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Slab-Like Stones
metas.note: In the mountainous parts of Neamț county, stone walls and foundations are also common, but with a more slab-like appearance.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Small Bricks
metas.note: Houses made entirely of comparatively small bricks are common in hilly regions in western Romania.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Spike Finials
metas.note: In Dâmbovița, Vâlcea and Argeș counties you can commonly find simple, spike-shaped roof ornaments.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Stone Crosses
metas.note: In the far north-west in Satu Mare county, you can find these bold, stone crosses on people’s properties
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Suceava Barns
metas.note: Traditional barns with asymmetrical roofs are found in the flat parts of Suceava county.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Suceava Colours
metas.note: In parts of Suceava county you will very often find unique shades of certain colours. The most important bright orange and dark red, commonly used in various elements of construction. Pale yellow and industrial green are less common, but also indicative of Suceava.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Suceava Gates
metas.note: Suceava often has traditional wooden gates similar to Maramureș, but usually with metal roofs. Suceava gates are also painted most times, as opposed to the wooden colour of Maramureș gates and have finer filigree detailing.
metas.footer: Note: Most gates have metal roofs with finials. However, roofs with shingles can also be found.

metas.name: Architecture - Suceava Stripes
metas.note: Suceava County has a lot of traditional houses with many unique features. One of these is vertical stripes that decorate either the gables or walls of houses. The ‘sun’ pattern on the gable in the image is also a Suceava meta.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Suceava Wells
metas.note: Personal wells are also very common in Suceava, usually with this very unique roof shape.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Székely Churches
metas.note: In Székelyland you can find all white, traditional churches (occasionally with yellow features), usually with simple spires, which are clearly non-Orthodox, as most Székely are catholic or calvinist.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Székely Gates
metas.note: Ornate wooden gates are also common in Székler-populated areas (see Székely), the key differences being the lack of a roof over the vehicle gate, and little pencil-top turrets on the side.
metas.footer: Worth knowing: The Szeklers are a Hungarian Szekler-speaking ethnic group in eastern Transylvania in central Romania, who have lived in the region since the 12th century. The Szeklers role as border guards for the Kingdom of Hungary provided them with certain privileges.

metas.name: Architecture - Transylvanian Saxon
metas.note: Transylvanian Saxon architecture is very distinct and constrained to areas which historically had many German settlers. Distinguishing features include baroque façades with plaster decor on the gable (usually including crosses and the date of construction), jerkinhead roofs, and more square versions of the twin Banat gable windows. The placement of the houses is also very distinct especially in towns, as they are mostly perpendicular to the street and connected to each other by archway-shaped driveways creating a ‘wall’ the whole length of the street.
metas.footer: Worth knowing: The Transylvanian Saxons are a German-speaking minority of the Romanian Germans in Transylvania. They settled in Transylvania in the 12th century as part of the High Medieval Eastern Settlement. The majority of the Transylvanian Saxons emigrated to Germany after the fall of the Iron Curtain in 1989.

metas.name: Architecture - Triangle Veranda
metas.note: Roofs with a triangle-shaped extension over the entrance, usually intricately decorated, can be found in much of the northeast.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - Western Hills House
metas.note: These houses with stone foundations, small stairs and façades featuring lots of glass in a carved wooden frame are commonly found in the western hills of the southern plain, particularly in Vâlcea and Gorj county.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Architecture - X Barns
metas.note: In the foothills of the southwest, you can often find these open hay barns with X-shaped wall patterns.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Apuseni Mountains
metas.note: The Apuseni mountains form a bulge of mountains geologically unrelated to the wider Carpathians. These mountains are substantially less forested than the Carpathians, and in the southern Apuseni you will find more conical mountains of volcanic origin.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Braşov Area
metas.note: The area just south-west of Braşov is a unique flat area with distinct mountains in all directions but north. Rather than forming chains, here you will find many isolated but very tall ridge-shaped mountains.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Bucegi National Park
metas.note: Bucegi National Park has a unique high-mountain landscape with almost no trees and golden grass.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Buzău Hills
metas.note: Around the south side of the bend in the Carpathian mountain range, you can find a unique landscape of dry, craggy hills, often with an exposed, pale underlayer.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Central Hills
metas.note: Relatively bare, rolling agricultural hills can be found in much of the Transylvania depression, just east of the Apuseni mountains. Further east of this zone, closer to the Carpathians, the hills will be comparatively more forested.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Covasna-Harghita Plains
metas.note: Flat plains surrounded by hills cover much of Covasna and southern Harghita counties. These are higher altitude than other flat regions, and therefore have more of a dead feel, with fewer trees and more potato fields rather than corn.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Făgăraș Plain
metas.note: The Făgăraș plain is an extremely easy to identify landscape. It is the only dead-flat part of Central Romania, and has a wall of tall mountains to its south.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Landscape - Tulcea Hills
metas.note: Much of Tulcea is covered in low hills which combined with southeast climate and architecture can make for very unique rounds. Note that the western half of this area is covered in forested hills, whereas in the eastern half the hills are mostly treeless.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Vegetation - Blackberry
metas.note: Blackberries (Rubus sp.) can be identified as low-lying thorny shrubs with characteristic five-part leaves. They are found in the foothills of the central and western mountains.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Vegetation - Hoary Cress
metas.note: Hoary cress (Lepidium draba) can be identified by dense clusters of white blossoms and leaves that hug the flower stalk. They are found most often in three hot spots across the country, namely the counties of Teleorman, Constanța and Iași. Topography can be very useful to tell these three regions apart, generally speaking Teleorman is dead flat, Constanța has slight hills and wind farms will usually be visible, whereas Iași has larger hills and you can often see trees planted next to the road.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Vegetation - Mullein
metas.note: Mulleins (Verbascum sp.) are found most often in and around Vaslui county, but beware that they can also be seen randomly throughout the country.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Vegetation - Russian Olive
metas.note: Russian olive (Elaeagnus angustifolia) is a small tree or large bush characterized by particularly white leaves. It can be seen mainly in the east of the country. Be careful not to confuse it with the more common white willow (Salix alba), Russian olive has comparatively whiter leaves and tends to be more unruly-looking.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord

metas.name: Vegetation - Vineyards
metas.note: While small, individual vineyards can be found all over the place, large concentrations of vineyards are mostly unique to the foothills just west of Focşani. Large vineyards can occasionally be found in the southeast just west of Constanța.
metas.footer: Based on Real Meta Research Group Romania Guide Join our Discord Real Meta Research Group Discord
